Head: Logic
Path: 一. Logic
Gloss: The structure of reality and, in the same concepts, of thought: the basic determinations all thinking relies on, each leading to the next. Then the study of these concepts in their own right and in that order.
Hegelian gloss: The science of the pure idea, of thought as the self-movement of the concept, in which the determinations of thought are at once the determinations of things.

Head: Doctrine of Being
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being
Gloss: The study of the simplest concepts, those that describe a thing directly as it is, without reference to anything behind it. Each such concept, when thought through, gives way to another.
Hegelian gloss: The sphere of immediacy, where each determination simply is and passes over into another; the concept only in itself.
Nouns: doctrine of being; logic of being, ontology; immediacy, directness, givenness, the given, datum, data; surface, face value; transition, passing over; change into another &c (becoming) H0007, rectilinearity†. the in-itself; being-in-itself; the concept in itself, latency, implicitness, potentiality; first sphere, outset, threshold. categories of being, immediate categories; what simply is, what there is; brute fact, plain fact, bare fact. beginning, commencement, inception. the sphere of immediacy, quality quantity and measure. esse, ens.

Head: Determinateness (Quality)
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality)
Gloss: The character that makes a thing what it is, so that if the character changes the thing becomes something else; the most basic kind of definiteness.

Head: Becoming
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › α. Being › c. Becoming
Gloss: Change at its most basic: the passing of being into nothing and of nothing into being. The first concept with real content, since it holds both together.

Head: Determinate Being in General
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › a. Determinate Being as Such › i. Determinate Being in General
Gloss: Existence that carries a negation within it, since to be definitely one thing is not to be others; being and not-being held together in the form of simple being.
Hegelian gloss: Being with non-being taken up into its simple unity, so that its determinateness has the form of being.
Nouns: determinate being in general; existence with a limit, being with negation; being and nonbeing united; finite existence; something rather than nothing; definite being, specific being; negation within being; inner limit, inherent bound; the being of a thing as distinct from other things; this rather than that. being-there in general, determinacy. quale.
Verbs: be something, be this rather than that; exclude, rule out, not be other; bear a limit within oneself. be there, exist definitely.
Adjective: definite, determinate, specific, particular, limited, bounded, circumscribed; negative in part, exclusive; finite. precise, well-defined.
Adverbs: in general; generally speaking, by and large, in the main. definitely, there.
Foreign: German: überhaupt; Latin: determinatio negatio est [Spinoza, Letter 50], omnis determinatio est negatio [Hegel's form of it].
Phrases: determinatio negatio est [Lat.] [Spinoza]; something rather than nothing; why is there something rather than nothing? [Leibniz]; of that ilk; to a degree.

Head: Quality
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › a. Determinate Being as Such › ii. Quality
Gloss: The definite character of an existing thing. It marks out what the thing is, and by the same token what it is not.
Hegelian gloss: Determinateness as immediately existing, one with being; as reality and as negation, since every determination is a negation.
Nouns: quality; character, feature, trait, attribute, property, mark, note, characteristic; reality, positivity, affirmation, affirmativeness, positiveness; negation, negativity, privation, exclusion, absence, lack, defect, want, shortfall, deficiency, limitation &c H0026. accident; attribute; affirmation and negation. lineament. particularity, peculiarity. actuality. determinacy, reality and negation, suchness. deficit, shortage. realitas. firstness [Peirce].
Verbs: qualify, characterize, mark; affirm, posit, assert; negate, deny, exclude, rule out, lack, want, fall short of. determine.
Adjective: qualitative, characteristic, attributive; real, positive, affirmative; negative, privative, exclusive, apophatic; partial, one-sided. qualified, determinate.
Adverbs: positively, negatively; in reality, in point of fact; in part, partly. qualitatively.
Foreign: German: Realität, Negation, Wirklichkeit, Wesenheit, Sachheit; Latin: accidens, via affirmativa and via negativa, actualitas, forma, formalitas, entitas, entitas quidditativa; Greek: symbebēkos, kataphasis and apophasis; Sanskrit: dharma [property, characteristic]; French: réalité; Italian: realtà, realtà effettiva, effettualità; Spanish: realidad, efectividad.
Phrases: every quality is a limitation; the defect of a quality, le défaut de ses qualités [Fr.]; for real.

Head: Something
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › a. Determinate Being as Such › iii. Something
Gloss: An existing thing taken as a self-contained unit with a character of its own; the first notion of a definite individual.
Hegelian gloss: The first negation of the negation: determinate being turned back into itself, the beginning of the subject.
Nouns: something; a thing, object, entity, being, existent, individual, particular, unit, item, article, body, piece, bit; this, this one, haecceity, thisness; self, selfhood; being-within-self; negation of the negation; something or other. existent subject, bearer, substrate. substantiality, hypostasis, person, a being, an existence, substance, flesh and blood, stuff, substratum, matter &c H0239, corporeity†, element, essential nature, groundwork, materiality, substantialness, vital part. thing, still life, stocks and stones, materials &c H0760. aught. creature, somebody, some one. anything, anything at all, whatever. quiddity.
Verbs: be something, be somebody, amount to something, count for something; stand out, take shape, crystallize, materialize; individuate, individualize, particularize. specify. exist.
Adjective: particular, individual, single, singular, unitary, discrete, distinct, separate, self-contained, self-identical; concrete, definite, determinate, specific; real, actual, palpable. isolated.
Adverbs: somehow, in some sort, after a fashion; in particular, particularly, specifically. somewhat. slightly. at all, in any way, anyhow.
Foreign: German: Insichsein, Negation der Negation; Latin: aliquid, haecceitas, subiectum, id quod est [that which is] [Boethius]; Greek: ti, tode ti [a this-something], hypokeimenon; French: je ne sais quoi.
Phrases: aliquid stat pro aliquo [Lat.]; something is rotten in the state of Denmark [Hamlet]; a thing in itself.

Head: Finitude
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude
Gloss: The condition of being limited; having an end that belongs to one's own nature.
Hegelian gloss: The determinate being of something, which has its end in itself; to be finite is to carry the seed of one's passing away.
Nouns: finitude, finiteness, finity†; limitedness, boundedness, limitation, confinement, restriction, circumscription; mortality, transience, transitoriness, perishability, impermanence, temporality, evanescence, caducity, frailty; contingency, dependence, conditionedness; the finite, finite things, the creaturely, creatureliness; the human condition. limit &c H0020; end, term, terminus, boundary, horizon. transientness†, fugacity [Chem], span. limit, bounds, confine, bourn. termination, finis, last, omega. aught.
Verbs: be finite, be limited, be bounded, have limits, have an end, come to an end; perish, pass away, die &c (ceasing-to-be) H0009; be subject to time, be mortal. terminate.
Adjective: finite, limited, bounded, circumscribed, confined, restricted, terminable, measurable; mortal, transient, transitory, perishable, ephemeral, impermanent, temporal, temporary, passing, short-lived, caducous, frail, fragile, fallible, creaturely, earthbound, sublunary; conditioned, contingent, dependent, relative. provisional, provisory, deciduous, precarious, unstable, insecure. qualified, conditional.
Adverbs: finitely, within limits, within bounds; for a time, for the time being.
Foreign: German: das Endliche, Geworfenheit [thrownness] [Heidegger]; Latin: conditio humana, pro tempore, ad interim; French: condition humaine; Arabic: fanāʾ [passing away]; Japanese: mujō.
Phrases: memento mori [Lat.]; all flesh is grass [Bible]; vita brevis, ars longa [Lat.] [Hippocrates]; we are such stuff as dreams are made on [Tempest]; mono no aware [Jap.]; something and its other; for good and all.

Head: Something and Other
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › i. Something and Other
Gloss: The relation of a thing to what it is not. Each side is "something" and each is the "other" of the other, so which is which depends on point of view.
Hegelian gloss: Something and its other, each equally a something and an other, so that otherness falls within something itself.
Nouns: something and other; the other, otherness, alterity; difference &c H0099; the alien, the foreign, the stranger, the outsider; the not-self, non-ego; counterpart, opposite number, complement, foil; relativity, perspective, point of view, standpoint; being-for-other; being-in-itself; self and other, us and them, this and that, ego and alter. the something. alius.
Verbs: be other, differ, be distinct, stand apart; other, alienate, estrange, defamiliarize; relate to, stand in relation to; contrast, compare, set against. relate to another.
Adjective: other, another, else, different, distinct, separate; alien, foreign, strange, outlandish, extraneous, external; relative, relational, reciprocal, mutual, correlative, perspectival. not the same, unequal &c H0054. unrelated, independent. ulterior. interrelated, complementary.
Adverbs: otherwise, else, differently; on the other hand, conversely; relatively, from another point of view.
Foreign: German: das Andere, Anderssein, Sein-für-Anderes, Ansichsein; Latin: alteritas, alter ego, per contra, vice versa; Greek: heterotēs, to heteron; Sanskrit: anātman; Korean: taja [the other].
Phrases: alter ego [Lat.]; l'enfer, c'est les autres [Fr.] [Sartre]; je est un autre [Fr.] [Rimbaud]; one man's meat is another man's poison; the other side; one another.

Head: Determination, Constitution, and Limit
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › ii. Determination, Constitution, and Limit
Gloss: Three ways a thing is defined: its determination, what it is essentially; its constitution, what it happens to be through outside circumstance; and its limit, the boundary where it stops and something else begins.
Hegelian gloss: Determination, what something is in itself; constitution, what it is through its relation to other; limit, the non-being of each in the other.
Nouns: determination, constitution, and limit.
Adjective: qualifying, qualified, hedged, conditional, exceptional &c H0073.
Foreign: German: Beschaffenheit, Grenze; Latin: finis, terminus; Greek: telos, peras [limit]; Arabic: ḥadd; Korean: gyujeong [determination], hangye [limit].
Phrases: est modus in rebus, sunt certi denique fines [Lat.] [Horace].

Head: Determination
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › ii. Determination, Constitution, and Limit › 1. Determination
Gloss: What something is in itself and is meant to be; its vocation, kept up in its relation to others.
Hegelian gloss: Bestimmung, the in-itself of something filled with content and maintained against its relation to other.
Nouns: determination. vocation, destiny, calling, purpose, end, in-itself, inner nature. destination, what something is meant to be, the vocation of man.
Verbs: determine, destine, ordain, appoint, fix.
Adjective: determined, destined, fated, intended.
Adverbs: by nature.
Phrases: die Bestimmung des Menschen [Ger.] [Fichte].

Head: Constitution
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › ii. Determination, Constitution, and Limit › 2. Constitution
Gloss: What something happens to be through its circumstances and its dealings with other things.
Hegelian gloss: Beschaffenheit, the determinateness something has through its being-for-other: its outward make-up, open to influence and alteration.
Nouns: constitution. make-up, condition, state, circumstance, situation, disposition, external character, accidental nature. habitude, diathesis†, fabric &c H0268, stamp, set, fit, mold, mould. category, estate, lot, mood, temper, aspect &c H0418, dilemma, pass, predicament. phase, position, posture, attitude, place, point, terms, regime, footing, standing, status.
Verbs: constitute, condition, dispose, frame, shape.
Adjective: constituted, conditioned, circumstanced, situated.
Adverbs: by circumstance.

Head: Limit
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › ii. Determination, Constitution, and Limit › 3. Limit
Gloss: The point where something stops and something else begins, which both separates and joins them.
Hegelian gloss: Grenze, the non-being of the other in something and of something in the other, through which something is what it is and also is not.
Nouns: limit. boundary, border, bound, bourn†, frontier, edge, margin, brink, verge, rim, periphery, confines, pale, march, marches, terminus, term, horizon, ceiling, threshold, line, demarcation, delimitation, circumscription, roomage†. bounds, enclave, curbstone†, but, reservation, termination, stint, precinct, backwoods.
Verbs: limit, bound, delimit, demarcate, circumscribe, confine, restrict, hem in, fence in, wall in, draw the line, mark off, mark out. inclose, surround &c H0228, compass about, hedge in, rail in, fence round, hedge round.

Adverbs: within limits, within bounds, within the pale, at the limit, on the edge, on the verge, on the brink, up to a point, so far and no further.
Phrases: ne plus ultra [Lat.]; hitherto shalt thou come, but no further [Bible]; good fences make good neighbours [Frost].

Head: Finitude as Such
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such
Gloss: Limitedness taken seriously: a thing whose limit is part of its very nature, so that it is bound to pass away; mortality, transience.
Hegelian gloss: The finite as such, whose being consists in having its limit within itself as its own end, so that its hour of birth is the hour of its death.
Nouns: finitude as such; mortality, the mortal condition, being-toward-death; perishability, transience, transitoriness, ephemerality, evanescence, fragility, frailty, vulnerability, precariousness, caducity; destined end, appointed end, doom, fate, lot; impermanence; vanity; the dust, dust and ashes; death's-head, skull, hourglass, guttering candle. finite things &c H0018. finiteness, limitedness, perishableness. terminability.
Verbs: perish, pass away, die, expire, decay, fade, wither, crumble, moulder; be numbered, have one's days numbered; be bound to die. cease to exist &c H0004, die out, disappear &c H0009. flit, vanish. end, run out.
Adjective: mortal, perishable, perishing, ephemeral, transient, fleeting, fugitive, evanescent, short-lived, momentary, frail, fragile, brittle, precarious, vulnerable; doomed, fated, foredoomed, condemned; sublunary, earthly, terrestrial, creaturely. transitory, passing. temporal, temporary, impermanent. finite.

Phrases: memento mori [Lat.]; vanitas vanitatum, omnia vanitas [Lat.] [Bible]; golden lads and girls all must, as chimney-sweepers, come to dust [Cymbeline]; all that lives must die, passing through nature to eternity [Hamlet]; et in Arcadia ego [Lat.]; all good things must come to an end; one's days are numbered.

Head: The Immediacy of Finitude
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 1. The Immediacy of Finitude
Gloss: The limited thing as simply given: something whose very being is to perish.
Hegelian gloss: The finite in its immediacy, determined only to perish, its passing away fixed as its unalterable being.
Nouns: immediacy of finitude; the merely finite, sheer finitude, bare mortality; fixed finitude, hardened finitude, the finite as absolute; despair of the finite, melancholy, sadness, mourning; perishing as essence; fatalism, resignation, acceptance of mortality; nothingness of the finite, nullity, vanity &c H0024. immediate finitude, the perishable, perishing, the hour of birth as the hour of death, the given finite. perishability, transience, caducity.
Verbs: be merely finite, be nothing but mortal; perish, waste away; insist on finitude, hold fast to the finite, cling to the finite. pass away, cease.
Adjective: merely finite, purely mortal, irredeemably finite; ephemeral, fleeting; melancholy, mournful, elegiac, resigned, fatalistic, epicedial†. transient, transitory, passing. perishable, immediate.
Adverbs: merely, only, no more than; in the end; irrevocably, without remedy. transiently, perishably.
Phrases: all is vanity and vexation of spirit [Bible]; out, out, brief candle [Macbeth]; sunt lacrimae rerum et mentem mortalia tangunt [Lat.] [Virgil]; born to die; the end of the line.

Head: Restriction and the Ought
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 2. Restriction and the Ought
Gloss: The limit felt as a barrier to be overcome, and the demand to overcome it. What a thing ought to be stands against what it is.
Hegelian gloss: The limit as a restriction (Schranke) within something, and the ought (Sollen) that is to go beyond it; each implies the other.
Nouns: restriction and the ought; bond. coercion &c H0712, cohibition†, repression, suppression, discipline, control.
Adjective: windbound†.

Phrases: ad astra per aspera [Lat.]; thus far and no further; occurrent nubes [Lat.].

Head: Restriction
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 2. Restriction and the Ought › a. Restriction

Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 2. Restriction and the Ought › b. The Ought
Gloss: What something is to be but is not yet: the demand to go beyond its own restriction.
Hegelian gloss: Das Sollen, the in-itself of something set against its restriction, which it is to transcend and yet keeps as its limit.
Nouns: the ought. ought, oughtness, obligation, demand, requirement, imperative, exigency, norm, standard, ideal &c H0849, aspiration, striving, yearning, longing, the gap between is and ought, is-ought gap, vocation, task, mission, calling, deontology, deontic.

Head: Transition of the Finite into the Infinite
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 3. Transition of the Finite into the Infinite
Gloss: The way a limited thing, by pushing against its limit, goes beyond itself and points toward what has no limit.
Hegelian gloss: The finite, by sublating its own restriction, goes beyond itself and in this going-beyond is the infinite.

Head: Infinity
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity
Gloss: That which is not limited by anything outside it; boundlessness.
Hegelian gloss: The negation of the negation: the finite's own going-beyond itself, which first appears as the infinite set over against it.
Nouns: infinity, infinitude, the infinite; boundlessness, limitlessness, endlessness, illimitability, immeasurability, immensity, vastness, unboundedness, eternity &c; the unbounded, the unlimited, the endless; absolute, perfection, plenitude. infiniteness, perpetuity &c H0232. infinity &c H0063. unlimitedness.

Head: The Infinite in General
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity › i. The Infinite in General
Gloss: The unlimited in its first, simple sense: what the limited passes into when it goes beyond itself; the negation of the finite, taken as what truly is.

Head: Alternating Determination of the Finite and the Infinite
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity › ii. Alternating Determination of the Finite and the Infinite
Gloss: The unlimited held apart from the limited, which makes it limited in turn; an endless alternation between the two, like a series that never arrives. Also called the bad or spurious infinite.

Adverbs: without end, on and on, again and again, over and over, round and round, back and forth, to and fro, hither and thither; et cetera, and so on, and so forth, and so on and so forth. backwards and forwards, wibble-wabble†. alternately. repeatedly, ofttimes†, unseldom†, not unfrequently†.

Head: Affirmative Infinity
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity › iii. Affirmative Infinity

Head: Syllogism of Existence (Qualitative Syllogism)
Path: 一. Logic › 3. Doctrine of the Concept › i. Subjectivity › γ. Syllogism › a. Syllogism of Existence (Qualitative Syllogism)

Head: First Figure
Path: 一. Logic › 3. Doctrine of the Concept › i. Subjectivity › γ. Syllogism › a. Syllogism of Existence (Qualitative Syllogism) › i. First Figure

Head: Second Figure
Path: 一. Logic › 3. Doctrine of the Concept › i. Subjectivity › γ. Syllogism › a. Syllogism of Existence (Qualitative Syllogism) › ii. Second Figure
Gloss: The form of inference whose connecting term is an individual instance.

Hegel definition: The mammals are the perfect animals: they have breasts, four articulated limbs and every organ developed. Because they suckle their young from themselves, they come to feel the unity of one individual with another, the genus, which exists in the offspring, though in nature this unity falls back into single individuals. They are classed truly not by marks we pick out but by the animal's own weapons, its teeth, feet and claws, by which it sets itself against its non-organic nature and shows itself a subject for itself. So there are four classes: animals with hands (man and the monkey), animals with claws (beasts of prey, rodents, bats, sloths), animals with fins (the Cetacea) and animals with hoofs (swine, elephants, cattle, horses), which can be tamed to work for man. Further subdivision is left to the contingency of nature, above all to climate.
Hegel quotes:
Mammals have breasts, four articulated extremities, and all their organs are developed. Because they have breasts, they suckle and feed their young from themselves. These animals thus attain to the feeling of the unity of the one individual with the other, to the feeling of the genus, which achieves an existence in the progeny in which the two individuals are precisely the genus, even though, in Nature, this unity of the individual with the genus falls back again into singularity.
— Encyclopedia §370, Addition (tr. Petry)
Of all animals, monkeys are the most docile (bildsamsten) and have most affection for their young; the satisfied sexual instinct persists for them in objective form, for they have passed over into an other, and in caring for the needs of their young, they have the higher, disinterested intuition of this unity.
— Encyclopedia §370, Addition (tr. Petry)
In mammals, the skin continues its growth into wool, hair, bristles, spines (in the hedgehog), and even into scales and armour (in the armadillo). Man, on the other hand, has a skin which is smooth, pure, and much more animalized and which also sheds anything of an osseous nature.
— Encyclopedia §370, Addition (tr. Petry)
Further essential classifications have been based on the behaviour of animals as individuals to other animals: that is, on their teeth, feet, claws, and beaks. It was a correct instinct which led to the choice of these parts, for it is by them that animals themselves distinguish themselves from other animals: if the difference is to be a true one, it must not be simply a sign which we have picked out, but a difference of the animal itself. By opposing itself as an individual to its non-organic nature through its weapons, the animal demonstrates that it is a subject for itself.
— Encyclopedia §370, Addition (tr. Petry)
On this basis, the classes of mammals are very accurately distinguished: αα. into animals whose feet are hands, man and the monkey (the monkey is a satire on man, a satire which it must amuse him to see if he does not take himself too seriously but is willing to laugh at himself); ββ. into animals whose extremities are claws, dogs, wild beasts like the lion, the king of beasts; γγ. into rodents, in which the teeth are specially shaped; δδ. into cheiroptera, which have a membrane stretched between the toes, as occurs even in some rodents (these animals come nearer to dogs and monkeys); εε. into sloths, in which some of the toes are missing altogether and have become claws; ζζ. into animals with fin-like limbs, the Cetacea; ηη. into hoofed animals, like swine, elephants (which have a trunk), horned cattle, horses, etc. The strength of these animals resides in the upper part of the body, most of them can be tamed to work; and the formation of the extremities shows a special relationship to the animals' non-organic nature.
— Encyclopedia §370, Addition (tr. Petry)
If the animals under ββ, γγ, δδ, εε are grouped together as animals with claws, then we have four classes: 1. Animals with hands, 2. with claws, 3. with hooves, which work for man, 4. with fins.
— Encyclopedia §370, Addition (tr. Petry)
[Lamarck, quoted:] The unguiculate mammals have four limbs, flat or pointed claws at the tips of their toes which latter do not envelop the claws. The limbs are, in general, fitted for seizing, or at least hanging on to, objects. These animals include those which are most highly organized. The hoofed mammals (Ungulata) have four limbs, the toes of which are completely surrounded at their extremities by a rounded, horny substance called a hoof (sabot). Their feet can be used only for walking or running on the ground; they cannot be used for climbing trees, or for seizing an object or prey, or for attacking and rending other animals. They are completely herbivorous. The mammals without hooves have only two extremities, and these are very short and flat, and shaped like fins. Their toes, covered by skin, have neither claws nor hooves (corne); they are the least highly organized of all the mammals. They have neither a pelvis, nor hind legs; they swallow their food without masticating it; lastly, they usually live in water but come up to the surface to breathe air.
— Encyclopedia §370, Addition (tr. Petry)
As regards the further subdivisions, these must be left to the chance and contingency proper to Nature, that is, to be determined by external factors. Climate, however, still constitutes the great determining factor. In southern latitudes, the animal kingdom is particularized more according to differences of climate and country than it is in northern latitudes: thus the Asiatic and African elephants are essentially distinct from each other, while in America there are none; lions and tigers, etc., are similarly distinguished.
— Encyclopedia §370, Addition (tr. Petry)

Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › a. Fancy › i. Observation
Gloss: The artist's gift for seeing the shapes of the world and keeping them in memory.
Hegelian gloss: The first side of Phantasie: the gift and sense for grasping actuality, which sees much, attends closely and holds the many images of the world in a retentive memory.
Nouns: observation; perception, a keen eye, an eye for detail, attentiveness, noticing, the observing eye, retentive memory, a store of images, knowledge of the world, study from life, life study, sketchbook, field notes.
Verbs: observe, notice, take in, study, watch, sketch from life, take notes.
Adjective: observant, perceptive, keen-eyed, sharp-eyed, attentive, watchful.
Adverbs: observantly, from life.

Head: Circumspection
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › a. Fancy › ii. Circumspection
Gloss: The clear-headed awareness with which the artist sorts, orders and masters the material.
Hegelian gloss: The waking Besonnenheit of the understanding: without it, without sorting and distinguishing, the artist cannot master the content, and it is foolish to think the true artist does not know what he does.
Nouns: circumspection; Besonnenheit, deliberation, presence of mind, clear-headedness, sobriety, judgment, discernment, discrimination, self-possession, control, artistic intelligence.
Verbs: deliberate, weigh, sort, discriminate, know what one is doing.
Adjective: circumspect, deliberate, clear-headed, sober, self-possessed, considered.
Adverbs: deliberately, advisedly.
Phrases: es ist thöricht zu glauben, der ächte Künstler wisse nicht was er thut [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics]; Gedichte wie die homerischen seyen dem Dichter im Schlafe gekommen [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics, as an absurd belief].

Head: Experience
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › a. Fancy › iii. Experience
Gloss: The depth of feeling and lived experience through which the artist makes the material their own.
Hegelian gloss: The depth of heart (Gemüt) and of animating feeling (Empfindung), which pervades and quickens the whole and holds the content in subjective unity with the artist's inmost self.
Nouns: experience; Empfindung, feeling, depth of feeling, Gemüt, heart, inwardness, lived experience, experience of life, a rich inner life, felt life, soulfulness, the animating feeling, concentration of heart.
Verbs: feel, live through, take to heart, put one's heart into.
Adjective: heartfelt, deeply felt, soulful, felt, lived, experienced.
Adverbs: feelingly, from the heart.

Head: Genius
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › b. Genius
Gloss: The artist's inborn gift for true artistic production, with the energy to carry it through.
Hegelian gloss: Genie, the general capacity for true production of art together with the energy to develop and work it out; it has, unlike thought, a side of natural gift.
Nouns: genius; native genius, creative genius, the gift, the born artist. genius, flair, brilliance, fire of genius, heaven-born genius, the divine spark.
Adjective: brilliant, gifted, ingenious.
Adverbs: brilliantly, by genius.
Phrases: a stroke of genius; poeta nascitur, non fit [Lat.] [the poet is born, not made].

Head: Talent
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › b. Genius › i. Talent
Gloss: A particular aptitude for one art or skill, as distinct from genius.
Hegelian gloss: Talent, the specific capacity for a particular art, which reaches full life only with genius; one may have talent and not genius.
Nouns: talent; aptitude, knack, bent, turn, specific gift, special ability, an ear, an eye, a feel for. talent, gift, talent &c H0474, ability, faculty, endowment, forte.
Adjective: talented, endowed.
Phrases: a good horse is hard to mount, but it carries you far, liang ma nan cheng, ran ke yi ren zhong zhi yuan [Chin.] [Mozi].

Head: Culturation
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › b. Genius › ii. Culturation
Gloss: A gift that is inborn yet belongs to a people rather than to one person, like the Italian improvisers' readiness in verse.
Hegelian gloss: Genius as Naturgabe: a natural gift which Hegel ties to the particular nationality of peoples, so that a people's art and its manner of production go together, as with the improvisers native to Italy.
Nouns: culturation; national gift, national genius, the genius of a people, Volksgeist, native gift, natural endowment, inborn talent, folk talent, inherited tradition, the spirit of a people, folk art, the vernacular, improviser, improvvisatore.
Verbs: improvise. inherit, grow up in.
Adjective: native, inborn, innate, national, vernacular, folk, indigenous.
Foreign: German: Naturgabe, Nationalität der Völker; Italian: improvvisatore.
Phrases: in dieser Weise hängt die Kunst und ihre bestimmte Productionsart mit der bestimmten Nationalität der Völker zusammen [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics].

Head: Sensibility (Facility)
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › b. Genius › iii. Sensibility (Facility)
Gloss: The ease with which the gifted artist executes the work, so that it comes almost into their fingers.
Hegelian gloss: Leichtigkeit, the ease of inner production and of outer technical skill: what lives in the artist's Phantasie comes as it were into his fingers, as our thoughts come into our mouths.
Nouns: sensibility; facility, ease, fluency, dexterity, readiness, deftness, felicity, the knack, the touch, a sure hand, technical skill, mastery of the medium, sprezzatura, practical feeling.
Adjective: facile, fluent, deft, effortless, ready, dexterous, sure-handed.
Adverbs: effortlessly, with ease, fluently.
Foreign: Italian: sprezzatura.
Phrases: was in seiner Phantasie lebt, kommt ihm dadurch gleichsam in die Finger [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics].

Head: Enthusiasm
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › c. Enthusiasm
Gloss: The inspired state in which imagination and execution become one.
Hegelian gloss: Begeisterung, the activity of Phantasie and of technical execution considered as a state in the artist.
Nouns: enthusiasm; Begeisterung, rapture, the creative state, possession, frenzy of creation. enthusiasm, divine afflatus, the Muse, creative fire, verve, aspiration.
Verbs: enthuse, kindle, inspire, be inspired.
Adjective: inspired, enthused, rapt.
Adverbs: inspiredly, with inspiration, in a rapture.
Phrases: sing in me, Muse [Homer]; divine inspiration.

Head: Origins of Enthusiasm
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › c. Enthusiasm › i. Origins of Enthusiasm
Gloss: Where inspiration comes from: not from stimulants or mere resolve, but from an occasion that brings a content.
Hegelian gloss: Hegel asks how Begeisterung arises, rejects sensuous stimulus and the bare will to produce, and finds it in an occasion, inner or outer, that hands the artist a content.
Nouns: origins of enthusiasm; the sources of inspiration, the springs of creation, the creative impulse, stimulus, spur, prompting, the spark.

Head: Boredom
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › c. Enthusiasm › i. Origins of Enthusiasm › 1. Boredom
Gloss: Waiting for inspiration to arrive by itself, through wine or idleness; Hegel says it does not come so.
Hegelian gloss: The belief that Begeisterung comes from sensuous stimulation: but champagne yields no poetry, and the best genius may lie morning and evening in the green grass gazing at the sky and feel no breath of inspiration.
Nouns: boredom; idleness, ennui, tedium, waiting for the Muse, lying fallow, writer's block, sensuous stimulation, stimulants, intoxication, champagne, dolce far niente, daydreaming, lassitude, torpor.
Verbs: idle, laze, lie in the grass, gaze at the sky, wait for inspiration.
Adjective: idle, bored, uninspired, listless, fallow, blocked.
Foreign: Italian: dolce far niente; French: ennui.
Phrases: Champagner giebt noch keine Poesie [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics]; die Wärme des Bluts macht's nicht allein [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics].

Head: Artistic Intention
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › c. Enthusiasm › i. Origins of Enthusiasm › 2. Artistic Intention
Gloss: Setting out to be inspired by an act of will; Hegel says this too fails without a living content.
Hegelian gloss: Begeisterung cannot be called up by the bare spiritual intention to produce: whoever merely resolves to be inspired in order to make a poem, with no content already alive in him, will make no fine work.
Nouns: artistic intention; resolve, intention, the will to create, deliberate effort, design, ambition, forced inspiration, contrivance, laboured effort.
Verbs: set out, intend, resolve, contrive, force it, strain after effect.
Adjective: deliberate, intentional, contrived, forced, laboured.
Phrases: weder jene nur sinnliche Anregung noch der bloße Wille und Entschluß [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics].

Head: External Inspiration
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › c. Enthusiasm › i. Origins of Enthusiasm › 3. External Inspiration
Gloss: The outside occasion that sets the artist to work: a commission, an event, a given subject.
Hegelian gloss: An external occasion, a commission or an event, which the genuine artist takes up and fills with his own life.
Nouns: external inspiration; occasion, commission, patronage, the patron, a given subject, prompt, assignment, the brief, occasional poem.
Verbs: commission, prompt, occasion.
Adjective: commissioned, occasional.
Foreign: German: Gelegenheitsgedicht.

Head: Theme
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › c. Enthusiasm › ii. Theme
Gloss: The definite content that seizes the artist and asks to be given shape.
Hegelian gloss: The determinate content, taken up by Phantasie, which is the true source of Begeisterung.
Nouns: theme; subject, subject matter, content, matter, topic, motif, argument, burden, material.
Adjective: thematic.

Head: The Project
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 1. Inspiration › c. Enthusiasm › iii. The Project
Gloss: The artist's full absorption in the work in hand, forgetting themselves in the matter.
Hegelian gloss: Begeisterung proper: the artist wholly filled by the matter and absorbed in it, letting no merely subjective particularity in, until the work is complete.
Nouns: the project; the work in hand, absorption, immersion, total engagement, devotion to the work, single-mindedness, work in progress, opus, magnum opus, labour of love.
Verbs: be absorbed, lose oneself in the work, immerse oneself, devote oneself.
Adjective: absorbed, immersed, engrossed, single-minded.
Foreign: German: Aufgehen in der Sache.

Head: Objectivity of Representation
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 2. Objectivity of Representation
Gloss: The truthfulness of the artist's presentation.
Hegelian gloss: The objectivity of representation, the artist's being entirely in the matter.
Nouns: objectivity of representation; objectivity, impersonality, fidelity, truthfulness, accuracy, realism, the work's own life. veracity, frankness, truth, sincerity, candor, honesty, plain dealing, love of truth, unreserve†. truth to the subject, self-forgetfulness, absorption in the thing, the matter itself, faithfulness. verisimilitude.
Verbs: depict faithfully, render, represent. objectify, render truly, efface oneself, lose oneself in the subject, be faithful.
Adjective: objective, impersonal, faithful, realistic, matter-of-fact. nonsubjective†. truthful, self-forgetful, disinterested.
Adverbs: objectively, faithfully. truthfully, impersonally.
Foreign: German: Sachlichkeit [matter-of-factness]; Latin: bona fides.
Phrases: the work speaks for itself; true to life; warts and all.

Head: Authorship
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 3. Authorship
Gloss: The artist's individual manner, the general style of the art, and the originality that unites them.
Hegelian gloss: The artist's subjective manner, the objective style, and originality as their identity.
Nouns: authorship. graphoidea†, graphomania†, phrenoia†.
Foreign: Latin: stylus, sui generis uncommon, arbiter elegantiarum [judge of taste] [Tacitus on Petronius]; French: la morgue litteraire, pasticheur, baroque, manière, faire; Italian: maniera, pasticcio [pastiche], barocco, stile; Sanskrit: rīti [style]; Korean: meot [flair, style]; German: Barock; Portuguese: barroco; Dutch: manjer, handeling, wijze van doen.

Head: Mere Manner
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 3. Authorship › a. Mere Manner
Gloss: The artist's merely personal way of doing things, which intrudes on the demands of the subject.
Hegelian gloss: Bloße Manier, the particular and contingent peculiarity of the artist, which Hegel calls the worst an artist can give himself up to.
Nouns: mere manner; manner, mannerism, the mannered, affectation, artifice, preciosity, schmaltz, kitsch. mannerism &c H0734, euphuism†, marinism†, kitsch [Broch, Greenberg].
Verbs: mannerize.
Adjective: mannered, artificial, affected, euphuistic†.
Foreign: German: Manier, Kitsch.
Phrases: die Manier das Schlechteste, dem sich der Künstler hingeben kann [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics].

Head: Idiosyncrasy
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 3. Authorship › a. Mere Manner › i. Idiosyncrasy
Gloss: A merely accidental peculiarity of the artist, which belongs to them and not to the matter.
Hegelian gloss: Manier as the artist's contingent peculiarity (zufällige Eigentümlichkeit), concerning not the general nature of the subject but only the particular artist.
Nouns: idiosyncrasy; quirk, tic, personal trait, foible, eccentricity, habit, signature habit. idiosyncrasy, individuality, peculiarity, idiocrasy &c H0403.
Verbs: individualize.
Adjective: idiosyncratic, individual.
Adverbs: in his own manner.

Head: Idiom
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 3. Authorship › a. Mere Manner › ii. Idiom
Gloss: A way of working that belongs to an artist and their followers and pupils, become habit through repetition; a school's manner.
Hegelian gloss: Manier as a mode of presentation (Darstellungsweise) proper to the artist, his followers and pupils, formed into habit by frequent repetition; it finds most room in painting and music.
Nouns: idiom; school, the manner of a school, house style, workshop practice, following, imitation, pastiche, convention, formula, routine, epigone, follower, pupil, disciple. idiom.
Adjective: academical†. derivative, conventional, formulaic, imitative, epigonal, academic.
Adverbs: in the manner of the school. in the manner of.

Head: Authenticity
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 3. Authorship › a. Mere Manner › iii. Authenticity
Gloss: A manner that has widened beyond private habit to keep to the nature of the matter, like Goethe's or Horace's light turn at the end of a serious poem.
Hegelian gloss: Die ächtere Manier: a manner that lifts itself out of narrow particularity and holds to the nature of the matter in a more general way, as Goethe and Horace end serious beginnings with a cheerful turn.
Nouns: authenticity; the truer manner, a personal yet general manner, the light touch, the deft turn, a cheerful ending, conversational ease. authenticity.
Adjective: authentic, genuine, natural, unforced.
Phrases: die ächtere Manier [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics].

Head: Style
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 3. Authorship › b. Style
Gloss: The way of presentation that the medium and the laws of an art demand, as distinct from an artist's manner.
Hegelian gloss: Stil, the manner of presentation that follows the conditions of the material and the demands of the art and its kinds, as in the severe, the ideal and the pleasing style.
Nouns: style; the laws of the art, the demands of the medium, the severe style, the ideal style, the pleasing style. style, diction, technique. phraseology, wording, strain, composition, mode of expression, choice of words, mode of speech, literary power, ready pen, pen of a ready writer, command of language &c H0662. turn of expression. hand, touch, the grand manner. perspicuity, perspicuousness &c H0662, plain speaking &c H0662, definiteness, definition, exactness &c H0214, explicitness, lucidness. obscurity &c H0662, involution, hard words, ambiguity &c H0662, unintelligibleness, vagueness &c H0667, inexactness &c H0214, what d'ye call 'em &c H0662 [Obs.], darkness of meaning. plainness, simplicity, severity, plain terms, plain English, Saxon English, household words.
Verbs: stylize. call a spade 'a spade', plunge in medias res, come to the point.
Adjective: stylish, stylistic. lucid &c H0662, explicit &c H0662, exact. obscure, crabbed, involved, confused. plain, simple, unornamented, unadorned, unvarnished, homely, homespun, neat, severe, chaste, pure, Saxon, commonplace, matter-of- fact, natural, prosaic, kempt†, tricksy†. dry, unvaried, monotonous &c H0662.
Adverbs: stylishly, with style. in plain terms, in plain words, in plain English, in plain common parlance, point-blank.
Foreign: German: Stil.
Phrases: le style est l'homme même [Fr.] [Buffon]; the style is the man.

Head: Originality
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › α. The Idea of Artistic Beauty › c. The Beauty of Art, or the Ideal › iii. The Artist › 3. Authorship › c. Originality
Gloss: The artist's own creation in which subjectivity and the matter are one.
Hegelian gloss: Originalität, the identity of the subjectivity of the artist and the true objectivity of the presentation, free of both manner and mere convention.
Nouns: originality; true originality, the original work, the new. originality, novelty, inventiveness, freshness, signature, voice. no imitation, creativeness, invention, creation. originality, invention.
Verbs: originate, innovate. strike out something new.
Adjective: original, inventive, fresh, creative, incomparable. unimitated†, uncopied†, unmatched, unparalleled, inimitable &c H0098, unique, untranslated, exceptional, rare, unexampled.
Adverbs: originally.
Foreign: German: Originalität.
Phrases: one of a kind; nothing new under the sun [Bible].

Head: The Forms of Art
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art
Gloss: The forms in which the ideal is embodied in art.
Hegelian gloss: The forms of art: the relations of idea and shape in symbolic, classical and romantic art.
Nouns: the forms of art; art-forms, symbolic, classical, and romantic art, stages of art, artistic epochs, modes of art. the particular forms of art, the symbolic the classical and the romantic, the forms of the beautiful, the stages of the ideal, the relation of content and shape.
Verbs: develop, evolve, succeed. form, embody, particularize, differentiate, unfold.
Adjective: formal, historical, epochal. particular.
Adverbs: in succession. in its forms, form by form, successively.
Phrases: symbolic, classical, romantic; in its proper form.

Head: Symbolic Art
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art › a. Symbolic Art
Gloss: Art in which meaning and shape do not yet correspond; art that hints rather than shows.
Hegelian gloss: Art in which the idea is still seeking its true expression, so that shape and meaning do not correspond; the symbol.
Nouns: symbolic art; symbolism, the symbol, the inadequacy of shape to meaning, mystery, enigma, striving, the colossal, the monstrous, Oriental art. the symbolic form of art, the pre-art, intimation, suggestion, the striving after form. hieroglyph.
Verbs: symbolize, signify, suggest, hint, strive. intimate, betoken, seek.
Adjective: symbolic, enigmatic, mysterious, colossal, monstrous, suggestive. symbolical, allusive, inadequate, ambiguous, Oriental, amphibolous†, homonymous†.
Adverbs: symbolically, enigmatically. by hint, by intimation, suggestively, ambiguously.
Foreign: German: Symbol; Greek: symbolon.
Phrases: the symbol is a riddle; the riddle of the sphinx; seeking its form.

Head: Unconscious Symbolism
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art › a. Symbolic Art › i. Unconscious Symbolism
Gloss: Symbolism in which meaning and shape are joined without awareness of their difference.
Hegelian gloss: Unconscious symbolism, in which meaning and shape are joined without knowing their difference.
Nouns: unconscious symbolism; primitive symbolism, natural symbolism, unreflective symbolism, myth, mythical thinking, nature-symbol. unconscious symbolics, naive symbolism, instinctive symbol-making, the undistinguished unity, original symbolism.
Verbs: symbolize unconsciously, mythologize. symbolize unknowingly, fuse, mingle, conflate, intuit.
Adjective: unconscious, primitive, mythic, naive. unknowing, unwitting, unreflective, instinctive, original, unapprized†, unweeting†, weetless†. uninformed.
Adverbs: unconsciously, naively. unknowingly, unwittingly.
Foreign: French: bricolage [Lévi-Strauss], pensée sauvage [wild thought] [Lévi-Strauss], science du concret [science of the concrete] [Lévi-Strauss], mythème [mytheme] [Lévi-Strauss].
Phrases: the myth-making mind; without knowing it; half-known.

Head: Immediate Unity of Meaning and Shape (Zoroastrian)
Head (German): Unmittelbare Einheit von Bedeutung und Gestalt
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art › a. Symbolic Art › i. Unconscious Symbolism › 1. Immediate Unity of Meaning and Shape (Zoroastrian)
Gloss: Symbolism in which the divine is directly one with a natural thing, as light.
Hegelian gloss: The immediate unity of meaning and shape, as Zoroastrian light, which is at once the divine and natural light.
Nouns: immediate unity of meaning and shape; Zoroastrian symbolism, light as god, fire symbolism, the sun, Ahura Mazda as light, Avesta. immediate unity, immediate identity of meaning and shape, the divine as light, the Zend religion, Ormuzd, the natural as the absolute, unseparated meaning.
Verbs: shine, identify, worship. coincide, be one, unite, fuse.

Adverbs: immediately, literally. directly, at one, without separation.

Phrases: light is the good; light is the god; the sacred fire.

Head: Fantastic Symbolism (Indian)
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art › a. Symbolic Art › i. Unconscious Symbolism › 2. Fantastic Symbolism (Indian)
Gloss: Symbolism in which meaning and shape are joined in extravagant and fantastic forms.
Hegelian gloss: The Indian fantastic, which drives natural shapes into the measureless to reach the divine.
Nouns: fantastic symbolism; Indian symbolism, the fantastic, the grotesque, the monstrous, many-armed gods, the extravagant, exaggeration, boundlessness, Hindu iconography, avatars, mythic profusion. extravagance, monstrosity, distortion, measurelessness, the colossal, riot of imagination.
Verbs: exaggerate, multiply, fantasize, extravagate. distort, inflate, run riot, ferment.
Adjective: fantastic, grotesque, monstrous, extravagant, boundless, profuse, many-armed. unusual, uncommon, rare, curious, odd, extraordinary, strange, wonderful &c H0672, denaturalized†. whimsical, fanciful, bizarre, outlandish. distorted, out of shape, irregular, asymmetric, deformed, misshapen, androgynal†, adelomorphous†, monoclinous†, unsymmetric†, crump†, misproportioned†, simous†, taliped†, talipedic†. exuberant, inordinate, superabundant, excessive, lavish. outre, preposterous, bombastic, inflated. vast, immense, enormous, overgrown. fantastical, exaggerated, wild, measureless. increased, asymmetrical, magnified.

Phrases: im rastlos raschen Überspringen von einem Extrem ins andere [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics, on Indian art]; a thousand arms; out of all measure.

Head: Symbolism Proper (Egyptian)
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art › a. Symbolic Art › i. Unconscious Symbolism › 3. Symbolism Proper (Egyptian)
Gloss: Symbolism in which meaning is hidden in shape, as in the pyramids and the sphinx.
Hegelian gloss: Symbolism proper, Egyptian, the riddle of the sphinx, where the meaning is sought in an obscure shape.
Nouns: symbolism proper; Egyptian symbolism, hieroglyph, sphinx, pyramid, mummy, the cult of the dead, Isis and Osiris, the phoenix, riddle, enigma, the symbol of symbols. puzzle, rebus. sealed book. the symbol proper, the genuine symbol, the hidden meaning, the mystery, the riddle in stone, the labyrinth, Memnon. hieroglyphics.
Verbs: encode, embalm, enshrine, riddle. symbolize, hide, conceal, veil, hint, intimate, enshroud.
Adjective: Egyptian, hieroglyphic, enigmatic, cryptic, sphinxlike. hidden, secret, recondite, mystic, cabalistic, occult, dark, acroamatical†, cryptical†. enigmatical, indecipherable. symbolic, mysterious, veiled.
Adverbs: enigmatically, in hieroglyphs. symbolically, in mystery, under a veil.
Foreign: Greek: hieroglyphika.
Phrases: sie ist das Symbol gleichsam des Symbolischen selber [Ger.] [Hegel, Aesthetics, on the Sphinx]; the riddle of the Sphinx; written in hieroglyphs.

Head: The Symbolism of the Sublime
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art › a. Symbolic Art › ii. The Symbolism of the Sublime
Gloss: Symbolism in which the divine exceeds every shape given to it.
Hegelian gloss: The symbolism of the sublime, in which the meaning is the one substance that exceeds every shape.
Nouns: the symbolism of the sublime; the sublime, grandeur, majesty, awe, the infinite, the overwhelming, the inexpressible. dignity, stateliness, solemnity, splendor, nobility, sublimity. the inadequacy of all shape, the beyond of form, the ineffable, the unfigurable, transcendence, excess, pantheism and the sublime.
Verbs: exalt, overwhelm, awe, tower, transcend. soar, know no bounds. exceed, surpass, overflow, outstrip, elude.
Adjective: sublime, majestic, grand, awe-inspiring, awesome, exalted, lofty, overwhelming. noble, high-minded, magnanimous. august, dignified, majestic &c H0537. high, elevated, towering, soaring, elevated &c H0238, insessorial†. imposing, solemn, transcendent, sacred. superb, magnificent. ineffable, exceeding, immeasurable. impressive.
Adverbs: sublimely, majestically. beyond all shape, beyond measure.
Foreign: German: das Erhabene, erhaben; Latin: sublimitas, sublimis; Greek: hypsos [Longinus], hypsēlos; Arabic: jalāl [majesty, sublimity]; Sanskrit: adbhuta [wonder].
Phrases: the sublime is the echo of a great soul [Longinus]; the heavens declare the glory of God.

Head: The Pantheism of Art
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art › a. Symbolic Art › ii. The Symbolism of the Sublime › 1. The Pantheism of Art
Gloss: Art that sees the one divine in all things.
Hegelian gloss: The affirmative sublime, the pantheism of Indian and Persian poetry and of Christian mysticism.
Nouns: the pantheism of art; the One in all things. artistic pantheism, pantheistic poetry, the all-one, the divine in all, the immanence of the One.
Verbs: merge, dissolve, unite, love mystically. pervade, immerse, lose oneself, see God in all.
Adjective: pantheistic, mystical, devotional. immanent, all-pervading, God-intoxicated.
Adverbs: mystically, in all things. pantheistically.
Foreign: Arabic: waḥdat al-wujūd [unity of being], fanāʾ [annihilation in God], ʿishq [divine love]; Persian: Ḥāfiẓ; Sanskrit: the Bhagavad Gītā, tat tvam asi; German: Entbildung [the stripping away of images] [Eckhart], Gelassenheit [releasement] [Eckhart, Heidegger].
Phrases: God in all things; a world in a grain of sand.

Head: Indian Poetry

Hegelian gloss: Die indische Poesie: Krishna declaring himself the brightest of lights and the best of each kind, the one essence in all its many shapes.

Head: Christian Mysticism

Gloss: The mysticism of Eckhart and Angelus Silesius, in which God and soul are found in one another.

Gloss: Art that exalts the one God above all creation.

Adverbs: sublimely, in praise. exaltedly, to the glory of God.
Foreign: Hebrew: Tehillim [Psalms], kavod [glory].
Phrases: let there be light: and there was light [Bible]; what is man, that thou art mindful of him? [Bible]; vanity of vanities.

Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art › a. Symbolic Art › iii. Conscious Symbolism of the Comparative Art-Form
Gloss: Symbolism in which meaning and shape are knowingly compared.
Hegelian gloss: The conscious symbolism of comparison, in which the separation of meaning and shape is known and their joining is the poet's act.
Nouns: conscious symbolism of the comparative art-form; comparison, simile, likeness, conscious analogy, figurative art, deliberate symbolism. conscious symbolism, comparative art, the comparative form, deliberate comparison, the known separation of meaning and shape, wit, ingenuity, the subordinate symbolic forms. figuration.

Adverbs: comparatively, by comparison. consciously, knowingly, deliberately.

Phrases: as it were; compare and contrast.

Head: Comparisons Starting from the External Object
Path: 三. Spirit › 3. Absolute Spirit › i. Art › β. The Forms of Art › a. Symbolic Art › iii. Conscious Symbolism of the Comparative Art-Form › 1. Comparisons Starting from the External Object

Head: Fable

Gloss: A short story or saying that conveys a general truth.

Gloss: A story of everyday life that points to a higher, general meaning.
Hegelian gloss: Die Parabel: an occurrence from ordinary life given a higher significance, so that the meaning is grasped through the familiar happening, as in the Gospel parables.
Nouns: parable. similitude, exemplum, moral tale. the prodigal son, the good Samaritan, story with a moral.

Gloss: A short tale used as an example to teach a moral, where the meaning is told openly.

Hegel definition: The laughable is any contrast between the substantial and its appearance, between an end and its means, in which the appearance cancels itself, so that realizing the end is the end's own undoing. Comedy makes this its principle. It makes the subject master of everything that counts as essential in what it wills, and lets its aims, being without substance, perish through its own willing and through outward chance alike. The subject does not perish with them: in their dissolution it enjoys itself, untroubled, as the infinite power over every finite content. In tragedy substantial ends destroy one another; in comedy what is null destroys itself, and the self survives it, cheerful, as the absolute. With this, art dissolves itself.
Hegel quotes:
Every contrast between something substantive and its appearance, between an end and the means, may be laughable; this is a contradiction in which the appearance cancels itself and the realization of an end is at the same time the end’s own destruction.
— Aesthetics, Dramatic Poetry: the principle of comedy (tr. Knox)
A world in which man as subject or person has made himself completely master of everything that counts to him otherwise as the essence of what he wills and accomplishes, a world whose aims are therefore self-destructive because they are unsubstantial.
— Aesthetics, Dramatic Poetry: the principle of comedy (tr. Knox)
[The principle for comedy is when] the mastery of all relations and ends is given as much to the individual in his willing and action, as to external contingency.
— Aesthetics, Dramatic Poetry (tr. Knox)
As regards the mental side of these phenomena, we know with regard to laughter that it is generated by an immediately obvious contradiction, by something turning at once into its opposite, hence by something immediately self-annihilating, -assuming that we are not involved in this null content, do not regard it as our own; for if we felt ourselves injured by the destruction of this content, then we should weep. If, for example, someone proudly striding along falls over, this can give rise to laughter over it, because he experiences in his person the simple dialectic that what happens to him is the opposite of what he intended. Hence what provokes laughter in genuine comedies also essentially lies in the immediate veering round of a purpose in itself null into its opposite; whereas in tragedy it is substantial purposes which destroy themselves in their mutual opposition. With the dialectic befalling the object of comedy, the subjectivity of the spectator or listener attains to a serene and untroubled enjoyment of itself, since it is the absolute ideality, the infinite power over every limited content, consequently the pure dialectic by which, in fact, the comic object is annihilated. Herein lies the ground of the gaiety into which we are transported by the comic. But the physiological appearance of this gaiety, which particularly interests us here, is in harmony with this ground. For in laughter, the subjectivity attaining to untroubled enjoyment of itself, this pure self, this spiritual light, embodies itself as a glow spreading over the countenance, and at the same time the spiritual act by which the soul repels the ridiculous from itself finds a bodily expression in the forcibly interrupted expulsion of the breath.
— Encyclopedia, Philosophy of Spirit §401, Addition (tr. Wallace and Miller)
